get_lease.reason: Its terms travel through get_tenant (space.lease) and its provenance through get_lease_evidence.
get_lease.finding: The correction's premise did not fully hold. LeaseIntelligence.CANONICAL_FIELDS has 13 entries; space.lease exposes 5 as values plus url/fileName, and tenant_name comes via space.tenantName. The remaining SEVEN — cap_base_amount, admin_fee_pct, gross_up_pct, expense_stop, audit_rights, pro_rata_method, renewal_options — carry provenance with NO VALUE anywhere in PropertyRecord. Measured: a tenant with admin_fee_pct 15 produces a response in which 15 appears nowhere.
get_lease.decision: Documented and deferred. The gap is in PropertyRecord, not the capability layer; closing it means extending the record, which is out of M5 scope ("do not redesign the architecture"). No second data path was built around the record to fetch them.

database_reads.per_capability: exactly three, identical for all four: /properties?id=eq.<pid>&user_id=eq.<uid>&select=id (ownership probe); /properties?id=eq.<pid>&user_id=eq.<uid>&select=id,name,sqft,data; /tenant_field_evidence?property_id=eq.<pid>&select=*&order=created_at.asc
database_reads.tenants_table: fallback only, inside the hydrator, when the blob carries no tenants
database_reads.asserted: E1-E6 assert the tables, the GET-only methods, the exact count of three per capability, and that each reports them

security_boundaries.identity: server-derived only; handlers take a token, there is no userId parameter
security_boundaries.only_id_read: user.id and nothing else — not role, app_metadata or user_metadata
security_boundaries.ownership: properties.user_id = authenticated user; tenant_users is never consulted
security_boundaries.retested_per_capability: owner succeeds, missing token, bad token, auth timeout, id-less auth payload, tenant-portal identity, caller-supplied userId, foreign property, missing propertyId — all four capabilities, not inherited from M4
security_boundaries.cross_property: the space lookup is a find() inside the owned record; no query in the module could reach another property
security_boundaries.generous_backend: the test database answers about the property for anyone, so every refusal is the module's own
security_boundaries.blank_token: refused without contacting the auth service

timeline_scoping_lost.byTenantCounts: null — an index of zeroes would read as "no tenant has any events"

unavailable_degraded_empty.space_uncomposable: section_unavailable, never space_not_found — the same rule applied to all four capabilities
unavailable_degraded_empty.spaces_from_table: degraded — the rows are real, the review state is not
unavailable_degraded_empty.hierarchy: unavailable > degraded > empty re-verified as a contract after the change (M1-M7)

full_regression.baseline_check: the same two assertions, unchanged since before M1b; not fixed, repinned or modified

m4_assertions_changed: K1 "three tools, and only three" -> M4's three are present, unchanged and FIRST, plus a new K1a that no name is registered twice. The original was correct for M4 and false once any phase adds a capability.

J1 the browser-API scan now reads code with string literals blanked. M5 added "never localStorage" to a provenance value, and a word-scan was flagging the sentence that promises the thing it checks for. A companion assertion checks that sentence is still present, so the check is discriminating rather than lucky.
deferred: Seven canonical lease fields carry provenance without values in PropertyRecord (see get_lease above)

No pagination or size cap; get_timeline and get_disputes return every row
get_space overlaps get_tenant by construction — in this data model a space and its tenant are one object; documented rather than disguised
